name: Directive had better

1.definition: Recommends a course of action, often implying an adverse consequence otherwise.

projection.target: Had can contract to ’d but ordinarily cannot be replaced by present have. The directive refers to prospective rather than past action.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Advice with had better
curious.summary: Had better recommends a course of action and often hints at a bad result if it isn't followed.
curious.body: In You had better bring the receipt, the speaker recommends bringing it. The words had better work together as a fixed unit, and the verb after them, bring, is in its plain form. The recommendation often carries a hint of what could go wrong otherwise, so it can feel stronger than a simple suggestion.
curious.try: Think of a time you gave someone strong advice. Could you have said it with had better?

teacher.summary: Helps explain had better as a fixed unit recommending an action, followed by the plain form of a verb.
teacher.explain: The directive had better is a VP with fixed had and better followed by a plain infinitival, as in You had better bring the receipt. It recommends a course of action, often implying an adverse consequence otherwise. This dictionary relates it to modal verbs with plain complements, because the verb after it is the plain form, as it is after a modal.
teacher.terms: This dictionary treats it as a fixed VP pattern related to modal verbs.
watch_for: A learner might add to before the verb, though the pattern takes the plain form (bring).
A learner might hear had as signalling past time, when the pattern recommends an action.
teacher.activity: Give students short scenarios (a rainy day, a test, a train leaving). They write one had better sentence advising a character, then add what might go wrong otherwise.

child.hook: What do you say when you really need a friend to hurry?
child.explain: Had better is how you tell someone what is a good idea to do. It can hint that something bad might happen if they don't.
child.play: Make a had better sentence for each picture in a story. Then say what might go wrong.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Directive had better." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/directive-had-better-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
